claimed_invariant: The DESCRIPTION SVEK plan is an ordered partition of renderable leaves by immediate owner. Groups are traversed recursively before root unpackaged leaves, but every leaf appears exactly once and every logical layout slot corresponds to exactly one accepted LayoutGraph node. Position remapping must be a bijection over that unique inventory rather than a counter over attempted insertions.
causal_divergence: The new groups-first Rust planner performs the correct explicit root-group recursion, but its final collect_owner(None) call also recursively visits root groups. Cluster leaves therefore occur twice in the plan. LayoutGraph rejects the duplicate add_node calls while the renderer still increments and stores later slot numbers, so valid nested DESCRIPTION diagrams panic when those nonexistent slots are read. Root-only inputs pass because they have no child-group recursion to duplicate.
planned_model_change: Separate owner-local leaf emission from child-group recursion. Traverse every top-level group recursively once, then emit only the root owner's direct unpackaged leaves and notes without descending into groups again. Treat LayoutGraph.add_node rejection as an invariant violation during plan construction so slot accounting can never silently diverge from the physical graph inventory. Keep groups-first order and the independent canonical node/note remap intact.
